topic: Wrapping WGSL uniform values in structs for wgpu bindings
principle: In wgpu, uniform buffers bound to WGSL shaders must match the memory layout expected by the GPU. Raw scalars passed as uniforms cause alignment and binding panics because WGSL requires uniform addresses to point to struct types. Always wrap uniform values in a named struct, even for single values, to satisfy wgpu's binding validation and WGSL's address space rules.
instruction: When creating a uniform buffer in wgpu that will be read by a WGSL compute or render shader, define the uniform data as a struct in both the Rust side (using `bytemuck::Pod` + `Zeroable`) and the WGSL side. Never bind a buffer containing a bare scalar (e.g., `f32`, `u32`, `vec4<f32>`) directly as a uniform — wgpu will panic with a binding layout mismatch or the shader will fail to compile.
